newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil senator seeks inquiry into debt fraud claim.
newsitem.headline: Brazil senator seeks inquiry into debt fraud claim.

text.p: A senior Brazilian senator said he was seeking to set up a parliamentary inquiry into suspected fraudulent debt operations involving state and municipal governments.
"I will ask for a Parliamentary Commission of Inquiry (CPI) to be set up," said Sen. Jader Barbalho, upper house leader of the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB).

Barbalho said he had so far gathered signatures from 17 senators of a total 27 needed to create the CPI which would look into alleged fraudulent requests by states and municipalities for authorization to borrow on financial markets.

Recents news reports have said at least two Brazilian states claimed they needed to borrow sums far higher than they in fact needed to pay off debts. Brazil's constitution states that such operations must be approved by the Central Bank and the Senate.
Barbalho said he believed "several billion reais" were involved in the fraudulent operations.

Sen. Sergio Machado, Senate leader of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's Brazilian Social Democratic Party (PSDB), said he had signed Barbalho's petition and the government was in favor of an inquiry.
